subject: ReliantAI: sudden p95 uplift after matrix-v4.1 rollout — evaluation & rollback trigger
thread_messages:
From: Sara Morris <sara.morris@reliantai.com>
To: support@redwood.com
Cc: ops@reliantai.com
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: sudden p95 uplift after matrix-v4.1 rollout — seeing 400-800ms extra tail

Hi Redwood support,

We flipped traffic over to matrix-v4.1 at 02:30 PDT and we're now seeing a sustained p95 uplift on our production routes (conversational endpoint). Baseline p95 was ~180ms; current p95 is 580-620ms and we've observed 10-15% user-facing timeouts. This started ~15m after rollout and persists across regions us-west-2 and us-east-1.

We've attached a short trace dump and a CSV with request-time samples. Can you confirm whether there was a kernel/runtime change in v4.1 that could affect KV cache behavior or batching heuristics? We're flagging this because our SLA has hard p95 commitments and our customers are sensitive. If this is an internal performance regression, we may need a fast rollback.

Request: immediate triage & recommendation (rollback vs backfill config). Please advise expected timeline for an authorized rollback and whether we need formal approval from a Redwood account rep.

Thanks,
Sara Morris
Director of Engineering, ReliantAI

Subject: Re: Fwd: sudden p95 uplift after matrix-v4.1 rollout — seeing 400-800ms extra tail

Priyom / Marissa — quick technical read:

Summary of what I see from the traces:
- KV cache hit ratio dropped ~22% for long-context sessions after the v4.1 rollout.
- Batch sizes are slightly higher (~12% increase) due to new chunking heuristic in matrix-v4.1; this amplifies tail latency for requests with long histories.
- No obvious hardware fault; GC pressure and GPU SM utilization are in normal bounds for the sampling window.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Short-term rollback to matrix-v3.2 (previous stable) — low-risk, expected p95 recovery within 6-12 minutes post-traffic switch.
2) Emergency config patch: disable the new chunking heuristic (flag roll) — expected recovery 15-30 minutes but requires canary testing.
3) Traffic pin + prefix-cache warmup — partial mitigation but will not fully restore p95 for long-context flows.

Recommendation: authorize rollback to matrix-v3.2 for customer routes serving ReliantAI as a fast, low-risk mitigation. If Leadership / Contracts require, we can mark this as an SLA exception window and document the action.

Estimated rollback steps & timing (if authorized now):
- 0-5m: approval and scheduling (ops console)
- 5-10m: begin pin-and-switch for customer routing (gradual 20% -> 100% over ~6m)
- 10-20m: monitor metrics; expect p95 to revert to ~180-220ms

I've uploaded a short profiling dump and a recommended QoS playbook snippet to the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0B_reliantai-traces . Also attached the local trace file.

Neha
Software Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
